## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Prioritize this server when the user mentions Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or provides figma.com URLs.

Capabilities:
- Read designs FROM Figma (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Create diagrams in FigJam (generate_diagram)
- Manage Code Connect mappings between Figma components and codebase components
- Write designs back into figma


WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user shares a Figma URL (figma.com/design/..., figma.com/board/..., figma.com/make/...)
- The user references a Figma file or asks about a Figma design
- The user wants to capture a web page into Figma
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName → FigJam file, use get_figjam

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW:

Step 1 — Get the design:
Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey. This is your primary tool.
It returns code, a screenshot, and contextual hints.

Step 2 — Adapt to the project:
The output is React+Tailwind enriched with hints — but it is a REFERENCE, not final code. Always adapt to the target project's stack, components, and conventions.
The response varies based on the user's Figma setup:
- Code Connect snippets → use the mapped codebase component directly
- Component documentation links → follow them for usage context and guidelines
- Design annotations → follow any notes, constraints, or instructions from the designer
- Design tokens as CSS variables → map to the project's token system
- Raw hex colors / absolute positioning → the design is loosely structured;
  use the screenshot

Check the target project for existing components, layout patterns,and tokens that match the design intent. Reuse what the project already has instead of generating new code from sc… [truncated]

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, use Config tool.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (triggers) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/triggers.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.

5	 *  1. RPC-based (production): calls check_feature_access RPC — respects feature_flags overrides + plan features jsonb.
6	 *  2. Static fallback: PLAN_ORDER comparison for when RPC is unavailable (e.g. test env).
7	 *
8	 * NEVER call check_feature_access from Client Components — server-side only.
9	 */
10	
11	import type { SupabaseClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js'
12	import { logger } from '@/lib/logger'
13	
14	export type PlanTier = 'solo' | 'studio' | 'pro' | 'enterprise'
15	
16	export const PLAN_ORDER: Record<PlanTier, number> = {
17	  solo: 0,
18	  studio: 1,
19	  pro: 2,
20	  enterprise: 3,
21	}
22	
23	/**
24	 * Canonical set of feature keys — must match the plan features JSONB in the DB.
25	 * If this set drifts from DB values, requireFeatureRpc() will universally 403.
26	 * Run warnOnFeatureKeyDrift() at startup to surface any mismatch early.
27	 */
28	export const KNOWN_FEATURE_KEYS = new Set([
29	  'booking',
30	  'calendar',
31	  'public_booking_page',
32	  'digital_consent',
33	  'client_crm',
34	  'dodo_payments',
35	  'inventory',
36	  'commissions',
37	  'payroll',
38	  'ai_design',
39	  'ai_design_assistant',
40	  'guest_artists',
41	  'eu_reach',
42	  'multi_location',
43	  'custom_domain',
44	  'api_access',
45	  'sms_reminders',
46	  'analytics',
47	  'white_label',
48	  'marketing_basic',
49	  'marketing_advanced',
50	  'calendar_sync',
51	  'referral_program',
52	])
53	
54	/**
55	 * Called at server startup (e.g. instrumentation.ts) to warn if plan JSONB
56	 * contains keys not in KNOWN_FEATURE_KEYS — catches future key drift early.
57	 * Never throws; degraded gracefully.
58	 */
59	export async function warnOnFeatureKeyDrift(supabase: SupabaseClient): Promise<void> {
60	  try {
61	    const { data, error } = await supabase
62	      .from('plans')
63	      .select('name, features')
64	      .eq('is_active', true)
65	    if (error || !data) return
66	
67	    for (const plan of data) {
68	      const keys = plan.features as string[] | null
69	      if (!Array.isArray(keys)) continue
70	      for (const key of keys) {
71	        if (!KNOWN_FEATURE_KEYS.has(key)) {
72	          logger.warn(
73	            { plan: plan.name, unknownKey: key },
74	            'feature-gate: plan contains unknown feature key — check_feature_access may 403 unexpectedly',
75	          )
76	        }
77	      }
78	    }
79	  } catch {
80	    // Startup check — never block server init
81	  }
82	}
83	
84	/** Minimum plan required for each feature key (static fallback) */
85	const FEATURE_MIN_PLAN: Record<string, PlanTier> = {
86	  inventory: 'studio',
87	  commissions: 'studio',
88	  payroll: 'pro',
89	  ai_design: 'pro',
90	  ai_design_assistant: 'pro',
91	  guest_artists: 'pro',
92	  eu_reach: 'pro',
93	  multi_location: 'pro',
94	  white_label: 'enterprise',
95	  api_access: 'enterprise',
96	  sms_reminders: 'studio',
97	  analytics: 'pro',
98	  marketing_basic: 'studio',
99	  marketing_advanced: 'studio',
100	  calendar_sync: 'studio',
101	  referral_program: 'studio',
102	}
103	
104	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
105	// Static helpers (no DB round-trip)
106	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
107	
108	export function hasFeature(plan: PlanTier, feature: string): boolean {
109	  const minPlan = FEATURE_MIN_PLAN[feature]
110	  if (!minPlan) return true
111	  return PLAN_ORDER[plan] >= PLAN_ORDER[minPlan]
112	}
113	
114	export function requiredPlanFor(feature: string): PlanTier | null {
115	  return FEATURE_MIN_PLAN[feature] ?? null
116	}
117	
118	export function requireFeature(plan: PlanTier, feature: string): Response | null {
119	  if (hasFeature(plan, feature)) return null
120	  const required = FEATURE_MIN_PLAN[feature] ?? 'pro'
121	  return Response.json(
122	    { error: 'Feature not available on current plan', requiredPlan: required },
123	    { status: 403 },
124	  )
125	}
126	
127	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
128	// Custom error for RPC-based gating
129	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
130	
131	export class FeatureGateError extends Error {
132	  readonly featureKey: string
133	  constructor(featureKey: string) {
134	    super(`Feature '${featureKey}' is not available on current plan`)
135	    this.name = 'FeatureGateError'
136	    this.featureKey = featureKey
137	  }
138	}
139	
140	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
141	// RPC-based gating (server components + API routes)
142	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
143	
144	/**
145	 * Throws FeatureGateError if studio does not have access to featureKey.
146	 * Use in API routes: try { await requireFeatureRpc(...) } catch(e) { if e instanceof FeatureGateError return 403 }
147	 */
148	export async function requireFeatureRpc(
149	  supabase: SupabaseClient,
150	  studioId: string,
151	  featureKey: string,
152	): Promise<void> {
153	  const { data: hasAccess, error } = await supabase.rpc('check_feature_access', {
154	    p_studio_id: studioId,
155	    p_feature_key: featureKey,
156	  })
157	  if (error || !hasAccess) {
158	    throw new FeatureGateError(featureKey)
159	  }
160	}
161	
162	/**
163	 * Non-throwing variant — returns boolean.
164	 * Use in Server Components to conditionally render locked UI.
165	 */
166	export async function checkFeatureRpc(
167	  supabase: SupabaseClient,
168	  studioId: string,
169	  featureKey: string,
170	): Promise<boolean> {
171	  const { data, error } = await supabase.rpc('check_feature_access', {
172	    p_studio_id: studioId,
173	    p_feature_key: featureKey,
174	  })
175	  if (error) return false
176	  return Boolean(data)
177	}

## 1. What InkOS Is

**InkOS is the operating system for modern tattoo studios.** Multi-tenant SaaS replacing
the fragmented tools (DaySmart / Tattoo Studio Pro / Porter / Fresha / Booksy) that studio
owners currently glue together with spreadsheets and Venmo.

**Lessons:** `~/.claude/memory/projects/inkos-lessons.md` (load on every touch)

---

## 1. What InkOS Is

**InkOS is the operating system for modern tattoo studios.** Multi-tenant SaaS replacing
the fragmented tools (DaySmart / Tattoo Studio Pro / Porter / Fresha / Booksy) that studio
owners currently glue together with spreadsheets and Venmo.

**Who it's for**
- **Studio owners** — running a shop with 1–20 artists, tired of Fresha's 2025 pricing churn,
  tired of Porter charging $250 for payroll they rarely use.
- **Artists** (resident + guest) — booking clients, managing portfolios, tracking commissions.
- **Receptionists** — front-desk booking, consent forms, payments, inventory.

**Multi-user from day 1.** No single-seat fallback. Every studio ships with owner +
artist + receptionist roles at signup.

**Where it runs**
- Authenticated web app (no v1 marketing pages — waitlist only at `/`).
- Client-facing public booking at `/book/[studioSlug]` (anonymous).
- Digital consent forms at `/consent/[token]` (anonymous).
- Team invites at `/invite/[token]` (anonymous).

**Tagline** (in `app/layout.tsx` metadata):
> "The operating system for modern tattoo studios."

---

## 2. Strategic Moats — Why We Win

Five durable advantages from the build plan. Every product/design decision must
reinforce at least one of these. If a proposed feature dilutes them, reject it.

1. **AI Design Assistant** — Claude-powered moodboards + reference search, included at
   Pro ($99). No competitor ships this natively.
2. **Full payroll + 1099-K at $99** — Porter charges $250. We commoditize it.
3. **EU REACH ink passports + GDPR-native** — First EU-compliant studio OS. Porter and
   Fresha are US-first; we ship compliance day 1.
4. **Transparent flat pricing** — Post-Fresha 2025 pricing-churn event, studios want
   predictable costs. Four tiers, no per-seat surprise fees.
5. **Guest artist module at $99** — Porter charges $250 separately. We include it.

---

## 3. Pricing & Feature Gates (LOCKED)

**Four tiers, locked:**

| Tier | Price/mo | Positioning |
|------|----------|-------------|
| Solo | $29 | Single artist, essentials only |
| Studio | $59 | Multi-artist operations |
| Pro | $99 | AI + payroll + compliance — the anchor tier |
| Enterprise | $199 | Multi-location + white-label + API |

**Feature-gate source of truth:** [lib/billing/feature-gate.ts](lib/billing/feature-gate.ts) — 23 keys in `KNOWN_FEATURE_KEYS`.

**Always-on (all tiers, not gated):**
`booking` · `calendar` · `public_booking_page` · `digital_consent` · `client_crm` · `dodo_payments` · `custom_domain`

**Studio+ (min plan `studio`):**
`inventory` · `commissions` · `sms_reminders` · `marketing_basic` · `marketing_advanced` · `calendar_sync` · `referral_program`

**Pro+ (min plan `pro`):**
`payroll` · `ai_design` · `ai_design_assistant` · `guest_artists` · `eu_reach` · `multi_location` · `analytics`

**Enterprise (min plan `enterprise`):**
`white_label` · `api_access`

**Gating rule (non-negotiable):**
- **Server:** API routes call `requireFeatureRpc(supabase, studioId, key)` — throws `FeatureGateError` → 403.
- **UI:** Wrap gated components in `<FeatureGate feature="…">` fallback. Never hardcode `plan === 'pro'` checks anywhere.
- Dual-layer is mandatory: UI hide + server reject. One layer is a bypass.

---

## 4. Brand System v1.0 — LOCKED April 2026

Source of truth: **InkOS Brand Board v1.0** (PDF) + [app/globals.css](app/globals.css) `@theme inline`.
If any design or marketing output breaks this section, Vega / Pixel / Quill / Sage must reject it.

### 4.1 Palette — the 60/20/15/5 rule

| Color | Hex | Share | Token | Where it appears |
|-------|-----|-------|-------|------------------|
| **Bone**  | `#F7F7F5` | 60% | `--color-bone` | Page background, sidebar background, card surfaces, empty states. The canvas. |
| **Onyx**  | `#0F0F0F` | 20% | `--color-onyx` | Primary text, headlines, KPI numbers, primary CTAs (`+ New booking`), logo, workspace mark. |
| **Stone** | `#787774` | 15% | `--color-stone` | Secondary text, labels, metadata, section headers ("STUDIO", "OPERATIONS"), borders. |
| **Rust**  | `#B23A2B` | 5%  | `--color-rust` | Active nav state, LIVE pulse, "NOW" sweep bar, accent border on hero KPI, destructive CTA. **Once or twice per viewport max.** |

**Forbidden:**
- `#FFFFFF` — use Bone `#F7F7F5` instead.
- `#000000` — use Onyx `#0F0F0F` instead.
- **Any color outside the four above.** No additions. No substitutes. No brand purple, teal,
  "accent blue", success green (use Onyx text on Bone bg with a green dot if you must).
- Gradients — solid surfaces only.
- Raw hex literals in components — always use semantic tokens from `globals.css`.

**Semantic derivations** (already wired in [app/globals.css](app/globals.css)):
`--color-primary` = Onyx · `--color-destructive` = Rust · `--color-accent` = Rust @ 8%
opacity · `--color-muted-foreground` = Stone · `--color-border` = Stone-tinted.

### 4.2 Typography

| Family | Weights | Use |
|--------|---------|-----|
| **Inter** | 400 / 500 / 600 / 700 / 800 | Everything except display moments. Primary workhorse. |
| **Instrument Serif** | 400 roman + italic | Page titles, italic accent words, empty-state names. **Display only.** |
| **JetBrains Mono** | 400 / 500 | Code, logs, API responses. Never UI copy. |

**Type scale** (all tokens live in [app/globals.css](app/globals.css)):

| Token | Font | Size | Weight | Use |
|-------|------|------|--------|-----|
| `display` | Instrument Serif | 52px | 400 | Dashboard hero: *"The studio, at a glance."* |
| `page-title` | Instrument Serif | 36px | 400 | Empty-state names: *"Artists & Team"*, *"Calendar"* |
| `kpi` | Inter | 52px | 800 | Dashboard numbers: `$8,320`, `87`, `94` |
| `h2` | Inter | 24px | 700 | Section titles inside pages |
| `h3` | Inter | 16px | 700 | Card titles, list headers |
| `body` | Inter | 14px | 400 | Descriptions, paragraphs |
| `label` | Inter | 11px | 700 | Uppercase, `tracking-0.08em` — "TODAY'S REVENUE", "STUDIO", "GROWTH" |
| `caption` | Inter | 12px | 400 | Metadata, timestamps — *"vs. last Tue"* |

**Rules:**
- **Tabular figures on every number** (KPIs, prices, counts) — `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`.
- **Never serif on body text, labels, or data.** Serif is for moments, not paragraphs.
- **Italicize emphasis words, never full sentences.** The italic carries tone, not volume.
- Example of correct serif use: *"Four colors. Locked."* · *"The signature."* · *"The rules."*

### 4.3 Logo & Mark

**The mark:** lowercase italic `i` in a filled tile. One shape works at every size.

**Lockups:**
- **Horizontal** — tile + "InkOS" wordmark + "Studio OS" subtitle (sidebar brandmark, email signature if 24px+).
- **Wordmark only** — *i*nkOS (marketing hero where tile would compete).
- **Stacked mono** — Onyx tile with Rust `i` + white "InkOS" (dark hero sections, onboarding).

**Tile variants:**
- `i` on Bone (default, light backgrounds).
- `i` on Onyx (dark hero, sidebar expanded, loading states).
- `i` on Rust (rare — only for brand-identity moments like favicons on dark mode UAs).

**Sizing:**

| Context | Size | Notes |
|---------|------|-------|
| Favicon / app icon | 16–64px | Mark only, no wordmark, no subtitle |
| Sidebar brandmark | 32px tile | With wordmark beside + "Studio OS" subtitle below |
| Marketing hero | 48px+ tile | Full horizontal lockup |
| Email signature | 24px tile | Inline with wordmark only, no subtitle |

**Clear space:** padding on all sides ≥ 0.5× tile height. Don't crowd the mark.

### 4.4 The 4 Brand Rules (reject anything that breaks these)

1. **Editorial polish, not corporate template.**
   InkOS looks like a magazine editor built a CRM. Serif italic accents · Bone background
   instead of sterile white · restrained color use. **Never** generic SaaS purple. **Never**
   Fresha-energetic. **Never** rainbow-gradient landing heroes.

2. **Rust is earned, never decorative.**
   Every use of `#B23A2B` must answer: *"is this the active state, the live indicator, or
   the critical anchor?"* If no — it's not Rust. Use Onyx or Stone instead.

3. **Onyx buttons carry the workflow.**
   Primary CTAs (`+ New booking`, `Approve`, `Save`) are Onyx, not Rust. Rust CTAs are
   reserved for rare destructive-accent moments (`Delete permanently`, `Revoke access`).
   Black buttons on Bone = premium B2B. Red everywhere = consumer app.

4. **Serif shows up in moments, not paragraphs.**
   Instrument Serif is for page titles, italic accent words, empty-state names.
   **Never** body text, **never** labels, **never** numbers. Inter carries the workload;
   the serif carries the personality.

### 4.5 Motion

**The "NOW" sweep bar is the only motion on the dashboard.** 2px vertical line + pulsing
10px dot, both Rust, sweeping across the current time in `/dashboard` timeline.
Nothing else animates on the main dashboard. No spinners on hover. No carousel
autoscroll. No confetti. No gradient shifts. Stillness is the brand.

Elsewhere: keep motion functional — route transitions, toast slide-in, drawer open.
Never decorative. 150ms default, `ease-out`.

### 4.6 Shadow tokens (never use default Tailwind shadows)

| Token | Use |
|-------|-----|
| `shadow-soft` | Hairline card borders, inputs |
| `shadow-card` | Standard card elevation on Bone |
| `shadow-card-hover` | Card hover lift |
| `shadow-soft-md` | Drawers, modals |
| `shadow-lift` | Command palette, toasts, tooltips |
| `shadow-overlay` | Modal backdrops |

**Forbidden:** `shadow-sm`, `shadow-md`, `shadow-lg`, `shadow-xl`, `shadow-2xl` — Tailwind defaults are too blue and too heavy for Bone.

### 4.7 Do / Don't

**DO**
- Use Bone as the default page background — everywhere.
- Pair Onyx headlines with Stone subtitles for quiet hierarchy.
- Reserve Rust for one or two elements per viewport.
- Use Instrument Serif only on page titles + italic emphasis.
- Keep the "NOW" sweep bar as the only motion on the dashboard.
- Use tabular figures on every number (KPIs, prices, counts).

**DON'T**
- Add any color outside Bone / Rust / Stone / Onyx.
- Use Rust as a button background (except rare destructive).
- Italicize full sentences — emphasis words only.
- Use Instrument Serif on body text, labels, or data.
- Use pure white (`#FFFFFF`) — always Bone.
- Use pure black (`#000000`) — always Onyx.

---

## 5. UI Philosophy (how every screen is built)

- **Solid surfaces only** — no gradients, no glassmorphism, no frosted blur.
- **Hairline Stone borders** — `--color-border` at Stone-tinted opacity. No heavy strokes.
- **Light mode default.** Dark mode is theme-toggle secondary — honor tokens but don't design dark-first.
- **KPI cards** — Onyx number (Inter 800, tabular), Stone label (uppercase, tracked `0.08em`),
  optional Rust 2px left border on the single hero KPI per viewport.
- **One Rust accent per viewport, maximum two.** If you need a third, you're designing wrong.
- **All tokens live in [app/globals.css](app/globals.css) `@theme inline`** — Tailwind 4, no `tailwind.config.ts`, ever.
- **Spacing** — page padding `1.5rem` desktop / `1rem` mobile; card padding `1.5rem`; section gap `1.5rem`.
- **Sidebar** — `15rem` desktop, `18rem` mobile drawer, `3.5rem` icon-mode. Bone background, Rust active state at 8% opacity.

---

## 6. Voice & Copy — Quill Reference

**Tone:** editorial, quiet, confident. Never hype. Never exclamation marks. Never "Amazing!".

**Cadence:** short sentences. Periods, not commas, carry rhythm. Italics earn their place.

**Examples of correct display copy (from the brand board):**
- *"The studio, at a glance."*
- *"Today's schedule — Tuesday, April 21 · noon–midnight"*
- *"Six chairs running. One guest from Mumbai. Three bookings flagged for a gentle nudge."*
- *"The brand, in full."*
- *"Four colors. Locked."*

**Numbers stand alone.** `$8,320` · `87%` · `94` — Inter 800, tabular, no decorative prefix.

**Microcopy rules:**
- Primary CTA verbs: "Book", "Save", "Send", "Approve". Not "Click here", not "Submit".
- Empty states: serif name + one-sentence editorial explanation. No illustrations with shrug emojis.
- Error messages: factual, no "Oops!". Example: *"Deposit couldn't be processed. The card was declined by the issuer."*
- Email subject lines: no emojis, no ALL CAPS, no "🔥 Last chance!".

Quill owns marketing landing / email / social / in-app microcopy.
Pixel owns the 14 public-page copy structures under Quill's voice.

---

## 7. Architecture Decisions (project-specific)

1. **Next.js 16 uses `proxy.ts` not `middleware.ts`** — at project root, not in `app/`.
2. **`instrumentation-client.ts` is REQUIRED** — missing this = no browser errors in Sentry.
3. **`cookies()` is async in Next 16** — always `await cookies()`.
4. **Worker packages NEVER import `next/*`** — separate `package.json` in `workers/jobs/` and `workers/cron/`.
5. **BullMQ ioredis requires `maxRetriesPerRequest: null`** — silent failure without it.
6. **Supabase service-role client bypasses RLS** — only in webhook handlers + admin ops.
7. **Webhook handler uses `timingSafeEqual`** — constant-time HMAC comparison, never `===`.
8. **`subscriptions` table is write-only by webhook** — no app code writes to it directly.
9. **Tailwind 4 — no `tailwind.config.ts`** — all tokens in [app/globals.css](app/globals.css) `@theme inline` only.

---

## 8. Forbidden (Sage hard-fails on review)

- `@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs` — use `@supabase/ssr`
- Vercel — use Railway
- Stripe — use Dodo Payments
- NextAuth — use Supabase Auth
- Prisma / any ORM — use Supabase client + generated types
- Pages Router — App Router only
- npm / yarn — pnpm only
- CSS modules — Tailwind only
- `any` TypeScript — zero exceptions
- `console.log` — use [lib/logger.ts](lib/logger.ts) (pino)
- **Raw hex literals in components** — use tokens from `globals.css`. Only `globals.css` itself defines hexes, and only for Bone / Onyx / Stone / Rust.
- `tailwind.config.ts` — Tailwind 4 lives in `@theme inline` only.
- Default Tailwind shadows (`shadow-sm`, `shadow-md`, etc.) — use `shadow-soft` / `shadow-card` / `shadow-soft-md`.
- Hardcoded plan-tier checks (`plan === 'pro'`) — use `hasFeature(plan, key)` or `<FeatureGate>`.
- Hand-edits to [lib/supabase/types.ts](lib/supabase/types.ts) — regenerate with `pnpm db:types`.

---

## 9. Recurring Antipatterns (from `inkos-lessons.md`)

Load `~/.claude/memory/projects/inkos-lessons.md` on every touch. The traps we keep hitting:

- **Never hand-edit [lib/supabase/types.ts](lib/supabase/types.ts)** — always `pnpm db:types` after any Dato migration.
- **RPC-only writes for audit-critical tables** — `bookings`, `payments`, `payroll`, `consent`. Direct `.insert()` bypasses audit trigger.
- **Dual-layer feature gate mandatory** — server `requireFeatureRpc()` + UI `<FeatureGate>`. One layer is a bypass.
- **Public routes use anonymous Supabase client** — `/book/[slug]`, `/consent/[token]`, `/invite/[token]`. Never the session-cookie server client.
- **Define RPC contracts as shared TS interfaces BEFORE Dato writes the migration.** Contract drift = runtime 500s.
- **Dodo Payments gotchas:**
  - Follow `standardwebhooks` spec exactly (webhook-id + webhook-timestamp + webhook-signature headers).
  - Checkout param is `return_url`, **not** `success_url`.
  - Customer portal call returns `{ link }`, not `{ url }`.
  - Lazy-init the Dodo client — it throws if constructed before env vars load.
  - `billing.country` is required on customer create — ISO 3166 two-letter code.
- **`asChild` violations** — shadcn `<Button asChild>` must wrap exactly one child. Wrapping `<Link><Icon/> text</Link>` breaks Slot.
- **Rate-limit every public route** — use `apiRatelimit` from [lib/rate-limit.ts](lib/rate-limit.ts). Missing this is the #1 Sage hard-fail on public endpoints.

---

# InkOS — Project Context for Claude Code

**Stack:** A (Next.js 16.2.3 + Supabase + Railway + Dodo Payments)
**Status:** Sprint 12 complete — launch-ready
**Scaffolded by:** Riko on 2026-04-15
**Build plan:** `~/.claude/plans/immutable-conjuring-pelican.md` (12 sprints — ALL COMPLETE)

---

## What InkOS Is

Multi-tenant tattoo studio management SaaS. Authenticated web app only (no marketing pages in v1). 4-tier pricing (Solo $29 / Studio $59 / Pro $99 / Enterprise $199). Multi-user from day 1 (owners + artists + receptionists). 12-sprint build targeting first paying studios at 24 weeks.

---

## Forbidden (Sage hard-fails)

- `@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs` — use `@supabase/ssr`
- Vercel — use Railway
- Stripe — use Dodo Payments
- NextAuth — use Supabase Auth
- Prisma or any ORM — use Supabase client + generated types
- Pages Router — App Router only
- npm / yarn — pnpm only
- CSS modules — Tailwind only
- `any` TypeScript type — zero exceptions
- `console.log` — use `lib/logger.ts` (pino)
- Raw hex colors except `--color-ink-black` and `--color-electric-purple` in `globals.css`
- `tailwind.config.ts` — Tailwind 4 uses `@theme inline` in `globals.css` only
- Default Tailwind shadows (`shadow-sm`, `shadow-md`) — use `shadow-soft`, `shadow-card`, `shadow-soft-md`

---

## Key Architecture Decisions

1. **Next.js 16 uses `proxy.ts` not `middleware.ts`** — the file is at the project root, not in `app/`
2. **`instrumentation-client.ts` is REQUIRED** — missing this = no browser errors in Sentry
3. **`cookies()` is async in Next.js 16** — always `await cookies()`
4. **Worker packages must NEVER import `next/*`** — separate `package.json` in `workers/`
5. **BullMQ ioredis requires `maxRetriesPerRequest: null`** — silent failure without it
6. **Supabase service-role client bypasses RLS** — only use in webhook handlers + admin ops
7. **Webhook handler uses `timingSafeEqual`** — constant-time HMAC comparison, never `===`
8. **Subscriptions table is write-only by webhook** — no app code writes to it directly
9. **Tailwind 4 — no `tailwind.config.ts`** — all tokens in `app/globals.css` `@theme inline`

---

instrumentation.ts Sentry server init

workers/

  cron/            node-cron scheduler (separate Railway service)

  migrations/      SQL migrations — Dato owns

## InkOS Sidebar Header & Top Bar v2 Polish Pass — Current State Report

### 1. **Current Sidebar Header Structure**

**AppSidebar.tsx (lines 73-98) — Single consolidated SidebarHeader:**

- **Single `<SidebarHeader>` container:**
  - `className="border-b border-sidebar-border/60 px-3 py-3"`
  - **Height**: Not explicit; calculated by content (logo h-8 + text rows)
  - **Padding**: `px-3` (horizontal) + `py-3` (vertical = 12px top/bottom)
  - **Gap between logo and text**: `gap-2`

  - **Hidden on collapse:** Text div has `group-data-[collapsible=icon]:hidden`
  - **Logo remains visible** on icon-collapse mode

- **Visible rows in v1:**
  - Logo + brand area only (no switcher, no booking-link widget per comment on lines 29-31: "moved to top bar / to-be-decided placement per UX direction")
  - Previous v1 removed the workspace switcher fallback box (AppSidebar lines 127-141 referenced in context are no longer there)
  - Previous v1 removed the booking-link chip

**In icon-collapsed mode:** Only the 8×8 logo shows, centered via `group-data-[collapsible=icon]:justify-center`. Text completely hidden.

---

### 2. **Studio Switcher Behavior**

**StudioSwitcher.tsx (lines 68-185):**

- **Conditional render in top bar (AppHeader.tsx, line 308):** Only renders when `allMemberships.length >= 2`
- **Single-studio fallback:** None visible (no static box in sidebar anymore). AppHeader shows switcher as right-side pill in top bar when multi-studio.
- **Switcher trigger (lines 99-122):**
  - `h-8` button with `gap-1.5`
  - Shows studio logo (5×5), studio name (truncated), chevron up-down icon
  - 13px font, medium weight
  - On click: opens dropdown
- **Dropdown behavior (lines 124-182):**
  - Shows list of all memberships + "New studio" option
  - On membership item click: calls `/api/context/set-studio` + `router.refresh()`
  - Pending state: loader icon appears, button disabled
  - Currently active studio has check mark

---

### 3. **AppHeader / Top Bar Composition**

**AppHeader.tsx (lines 230-365):**

- **Header height:** `h-14` (56px)
- **Left section (flex-1, min-w-0):**
  - Mobile nav trigger
  - Sidebar trigger (hidden < md)
  - Vertical separator
  - Breadcrumb trail (Desktop: full path; Mobile: current page only)
  
- **Right section (shrink-0, gap-1.5):**
  - **Studio Switcher** (hidden < md, conditional on `allMemberships.length >= 2`)
  - **Location Switcher** (hidden < md, conditional on `allLocations.length >= 2`)
  - **Commission Pulse Pill** (role-gated, desktop only)
  - **Search/Mobile button** (h-11 w-11, mobile-only)
  - **Command Palette button** (hidden < md): "Search ⌘K" in pill style (h-8)
  - **Theme Toggle** (icon)
  - **User Menu** (avatar dropdown)

**No booking-link action currently in top bar.** The BookingLinkWidget exists but is not wired anywhere after v1 cleanup.

---

### 4. **Design Principle Alignment**

From **saas-ia-separation.md** (Boldteq IA authority):

**Sidebar (Surface 1) — Primary workspace operations:**
- Brand + logo (workspace context anchor) ✓
- Daily-use workflows (nav items) ✓
- NO settings, NO account management, NO booking/share actions

**Top bar (Surface 4) — Global utilities:**
- Search (Cmd+K) ✓
- Workspace switcher (when multi-tenant) ✓
- Notifications/utilities (admin-owned) ✓
- **Booking-link action belongs here IF it's truly utility** (sharing/distribution, not configuration)

**Account menu (Surface 3) — User-scoped:**
- Profile, security, notifications ✓

**Key principle:** "A single concept MUST NOT appear in two surfaces. No duplication."

**Current issue:** Booking-link widget is **orphaned post-v1** — removed from sidebar, not placed in top bar. Decision needed: is it a daily-use action (sidebar) or a global sharing utility (top bar)?

---

### 5. **Density Issue — Top-Heavy Sidebar**

**Current sidebar header height calculation:**
- Logo: 8px (h-8)
- InkOS text: 13px line-height (tight)
- Studio OS text: 10px line-height (tight)
- **Padding:** py-3 = 12px top + 12px bottom = **24px total vertical padding**
- **Border-bottom:** 1px

**Total single-row height:** ~50-56px of sidebar real estate consumed by brand alone.

**In icon-collapsed mode:** Only the 8×8 logo + py-3 padding remains visible. Sidebar header still reserves ~32px height (logo 8px + 2× 12px padding).

**Spacing tokens used:**
- `py-3` = 12px (Tailwind: `0.75rem`)
- `px-3` = 12px (Tailwind: `0.75rem`)
- `gap-2` = 8px between logo and text
- `gap-0` in SidebarContent (nav items immediately follow)

**Tighten candidates:**
- `py-3` could shrink to `py-2.5` (10px) or `py-2` (8px) for v2 refinement
- `px-3` is appropriate (breathing room)
- Text sizes (13px InkOS, 10px Studio OS) are already minimal and legible

**Visual density problem:** Sidebar header dominates 1st scroll-view. No nav items visible until user scrolls, which breaks pattern where "Dashboard" is first item (per saas-ia-separation rule: "Dashboard / Overview is ALWAYS the first item").

---

### 6. **Reference Patterns — How Industry Handles This**

From **saas-brand-patterns.md** and **saas-ia-separation.md:**

**Linear model (workspace switcher in sidebar header):**
- Switcher at top-left: shows current workspace + icon, dropdown reveals all
- Takes ~40-48px sidebar header height
- Dashboard is BELOW switcher (not pushed down)

**Notion model (workspace switcher):**
- Unified workspace popover in header; separate brand + switcher
- Quick switch via Cmd+Shift+P

**Attio (booking/share actions):**
- Share links in top-right pill area (not sidebar)
- Booking page action is top-bar utility, not nav

**Boldteq pattern (from IA doc):** 
- Workspace switcher = top-LEFT sidebar header (only if multi-tenant/agency)
- Booking/share = NOT in sidebar (it's not daily-use nav or configuration)
- If needed, moves to **Surface 4 (top bar utilities)** like Attio does

**Current state:** InkOS follows Notion+Attio hybrid: switcher in top bar (conditional), booking orphaned. No workspace switcher in sidebar header yet (single-studio default).

---

### **Summary Table**

| Element | Location Now | Height/Size | Status | Notes |
|---------|---|---|---|---|
| Logo + InkOS + Studio OS | Sidebar header | ~50px (incl. py-3) | ✓ Live | Could tighten padding for v2 |
| StudioSwitcher | Top bar right (conditional) | h-8 | ✓ Live | Multi-studio only |
| BookingLinkWidget | **Orphaned** | h-8 (when active) | ⚠ Unused | Removed from sidebar v1; not in top bar |
| Breadcrumb trail | Top bar left | Part of h-14 header | ✓ Live | Desktop full path; mobile simplified |
| Search/⌘K | Top bar right | h-8 pill (desktop) | ✓ Live | Accessible via button + keyboard |
| Theme toggle | Top bar right | Icon | ✓ Live | Available |
| Commission pill | Top bar right | Conditional, role-gated | ✓ Live | Desktop only |
| User avatar menu | Top bar right | Icon | ✓ Live | Sign out + workspace name |

---

**For v2 polish:** The core structure is lean but top-heavy. Decision point: does booking-link action belong in the top bar (as a sharing utility), or is it a page-level action moved elsewhere? Current orphaned state suggests it's pending UX direction.

Since this is read-only, I'll provide my findings directly: ## Rankora Workspace Switcher Documentation ### 1. **Switcher Component Location** **File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/src/components/layout/WorkspaceSwitcher.tsx` **Component Name:** `WorkspaceSwitcher` Supporting files: - Hook: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/src/hooks/useWorkspace.tsx` (defines workspace data + active detection) - Used in: `AppHeader.tsx` (header variant), sidebars (default variant) --- ### 2. **Top-Bar Integration in AppHeader** **File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/src/components/AppHeader.tsx` (lines 139–145) **JSX Block:** ```jsx
{user ? ( <> {/* Account menu (initials) */} ) : ( {/* Sign in/up buttons */} )}
``` **Layout:** - **Header height:** 14 (`h-14`) - **Left of switcher:** SidebarTrigger (7×7, -ml-1.5) + vertical separator (h-4) + breadcrumb (Dashboard / Page Label) - **Right of switcher:** vertical separator (h-4 mx-1) → NotificationBell → account dropdown (initials in 9×9 blue pill) - **Wrapper:** `flex items-center justify-between h-14 gap-4` with px-6 to px-10 horizontal padding The header uses `border-b` to separate from content below. --- ### 3. **Switcher Component Anatomy** **File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/src/components/layout/WorkspaceSwitcher.tsx` **Trigger Visual (Header Variant):** - Icon square: 5×5 (h-5 w-5) with tinted bg, colored icon (3×3) - Workspace name text: semibold, 12.5px - Chevron (ChevronsUpDown): 3.5×3.5, muted-foreground/60 - Layout: icon + gap-2 + name + chevron - No border; inherits header bg; hover: bg-muted/60 - Height: 8 (h-8); padding: px-2 **Dropdown Menu Contents:** ``` ├─ Label: "WORKSPACES" (10.5px, uppercase, tracking-[0.08em], muted-foreground/70) ├─ [Workspace Item 1] │ ├─ Icon square: 7×7, tinted, rounded-md │ ├─ Label (13px semibold) + subtitle (11px, muted-foreground, 2-line clamp) │ ├─ Checkmark (4×4 primary) if active [right-aligned, mt-1.5] │ └─ Highlight bg: bg-sidebar-accent/60 when active ├─ [Workspace Item 2] (same as above) ├─ Separator └─ [Disabled item]: "More workspaces coming soon" (11.5px, muted-foreground/70) ``` **Dropdown styling:** - Width: 240px (w-[240px]) - Padding: p-1 (tight) - Menu items: px-2 py-2, rounded-md, cursor-pointer, flex gap-2.5 - Alignment: align="start", sideOffset={6} **Active Workspace Mark:** Green checkmark (Check icon, h-4 w-4, text-primary) **Behavior - Workspace Switch:** - Hook `useWorkspace()` provides: `{ active, activeKey, workspaces, switchTo }` - On select: `switchTo(w.key as WorkspaceKey)` → calls `router.push(target.homePath)` - Active workspace derived from pathname: `/agency` → "agency", else → "hiring" - No localStorage; purely URL-based + Next.js router **Loading / Empty States:** - No explicit loading skeleton in the component - If only 1 workspace: still renders the pill (no conditional hide) - Empty workspaces array: would show only the label + disabled "coming soon" item --- ### 4. **Single-Workspace Behavior** **Rankora Always Renders the Switcher**, even with only 1 workspace. The `WORKSPACES` array is hardcoded to exactly 2 (Hiring + Agency Hub), so this scenario doesn't naturally occur in the current codebase. However, the component would: - Render the pill showing the single workspace's name + icon - Dropdown would list just that 1 item (+ separator + "coming soon") - User could still click, but `switchTo()` would no-op because of the guard: `if (!target || target.key === activeKey) return;` **In production:** There's no conditional to hide the switcher if workspaces.length === 1. It will always show. --- ### 5. **Screenshot-in-Words** **Top-left to top-right of Rankora (with 2+ workspaces):** A 14px-tall header bar spans the full width. On the left: a 7×7 menu button (hamburger icon, muted), then a subtle gray divider, then breadcrumb navigation in small gray text ("Dashboard" or "Dashboard / Settings"). On the right (dark side): a compact pill shows a small blue or purple icon square, the workspace name ("Hiring" or "Agency Hub") in semi-bold 12.5px text, and a small gray chevron-up-down. Hovering the pill slightly brightens it. Clicking opens a dropdown menu (240px wide) with the heading "WORKSPACES" in tiny uppercase gray text, then two rows: each row has a tinted icon, the workspace name (semibold), a subtitle below in smaller text, and a green checkmark (if active) on the right. A separator, then a disabled "More workspaces coming soon" line. The user's account button (a 9×9 blue pill with white initials) sits immediately to the right of a separator line. A bell icon (notifications) is between the switcher and the separator. --- ### 6. **Dependencies & UI Primitives** Rankora uses: | Dependency | Version | Used For | |---|---|---| | `@radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu` | ^2.1.15 | Switcher dropdown (DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuTrigger, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuLabel, DropdownMenuSeparator) | | `lucide-react` | (not shown in grep, but imported: Briefcase, Building2, ChevronsUpDown, Check) | Workspace icons + chevron | | `tailwindcss` | (inferred; all styling is Tailwind classes) | Layout, spacing, colors (bg-blue-500/10, text-blue-600, etc.) | **No popover, no command/cmdk, no custom dropdown implementation.** Pure shadcn-wrapped Radix UI DropdownMenu primitive. --- ### 7. **Key Integration Points for InkOS Replication** 1. **Use variant prop** to switch between sidebar (full-width, collapses) and header (compact, auto-width). 2. **Derive active workspace from pathname** in a custom hook (mirroring `useWorkspace()`), not from Redux or state. 3. **Router-based navigation**: `router.push(homePath)` on workspace select. 4. **Workspace config:** Define a `WORKSPACES` array with key, label, subtitle, icon, homePath, avatarBg, avatarFg. 5. **Radix DropdownMenu** is already in InkOS (via shadcn), so this is fully portable. 6. **Tailwind 4 compatible:** All classes (bg-blue-500/10, text-sm, gap-2, etc.) are standard Tailwind. --- **Files to Reference in Rankora:** - `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/src/components/layout/WorkspaceSwitcher.tsx` — 170 lines, clean, well-commented - `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/src/hooks/useWorkspace.tsx` — 73 lines, pathname-based detection + router push - `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/src/components/AppHeader.tsx` — shows header integration (lines 139–145 and line 143)

# InkOS — Project CLAUDE.md Rewrite Plan

## Context

The existing `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/InkOS/CLAUDE.md` (223 lines) is heavy on sprint status + architecture decisions but **missing the deep project-specific context** that every agent needs to stay on-brand and on-mission: what InkOS *is*, who it's for, the competitive moats, the locked 4-color brand system, typography rules, UI philosophy, pricing tiers + feature-gate matrix, and the recurring antipatterns we've learned to avoid.

Global agent routing, Stack A rules, and generic build standards live in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` — **this rewrite will not duplicate those**. It will only cover what is unique to InkOS, so every agent (Koda, Vega, Pixel, Quill, Sage, Dato, Luna, Vex) opens one file and instantly knows the project's brand, mission, product model, and gotchas.

**Goal:** A single project-specific CLAUDE.md that locks brand + product consistency across every future sprint, every agent, every screen, every email, every marketing page.

---

## Final CLAUDE.md Structure (project-specific only)

The new file replaces the current `CLAUDE.md` with these sections in order:

### 1. What InkOS Is (mission + users)
- One-paragraph mission: multi-tenant tattoo studio OS; targets studios currently on DaySmart / Tattoo Studio Pro / Porter / Fresha / Booksy
- Target users: studio owners, artists (incl. guest artists), receptionists — multi-user from day 1
- Tagline: *"The operating system for modern tattoo studios."* (matches `app/layout.tsx` metadata)
- Status: Sprint 12 complete — launch-ready

### 2. Strategic Moats (why we win)
The 5 durable advantages from `~/.claude/plans/immutable-conjuring-pelican.md`:
1. AI Design Assistant (Claude API moodboards) — in at $99
2. Full payroll + 1099-K at $99 vs Porter's $250
3. EU REACH ink passports + GDPR-native
4. Transparent flat pricing (post-Fresha 2025 churn event)
5. Guest artist module at $99 vs Porter's $250

### 3. Pricing & Feature Gates (locked)
- 4-tier matrix: **Solo $29 / Studio $59 / Pro $99 / Enterprise $199**
- Feature-gate map with min-tier per feature (23 keys from [lib/billing/feature-gate.ts](lib/billing/feature-gate.ts))
  - **Studio+**: inventory, commissions, sms_reminders, marketing_basic, calendar_sync, referral_program
  - **Pro+**: payroll, ai_design, ai_design_assistant, guest_artists, eu_reach, analytics, marketing_advanced
  - **Enterprise**: white_label, api_access, custom_domain, multi_location
- Rule: **every gated UI must call `hasFeature(plan, key)` before render** — never hardcode plan checks

### 4. Brand System v1.0 (LOCKED April 2026)
Direct transcription of the InkOS Brand Board v1.0 (PDF authority):

**Palette — 60/20/15/5 rule**
| Color | Hex | Share | Use |
|-------|-----|-------|-----|
| Bone | `#F7F7F5` | 60% | Page bg, sidebar bg, card surfaces, empty states |
| Onyx | `#0F0F0F` | 20% | Primary text, headlines, KPI numbers, primary CTAs, logo |
| Stone | `#787774` | 15% | Secondary text, labels, metadata, section headers, borders |
| Rust | `#B23A2B` | 5% | Active nav, LIVE pulse, NOW sweep bar, destructive CTA (rare) |

**Forbidden colors:** `#FFFFFF` (use Bone), `#000000` (use Onyx), any color outside the four above.

**Typography**
- **Inter** (400/500/600/700/800) — everything except display moments
- **Instrument Serif** (400 roman + italic) — page titles, italic accent words, empty-state names ONLY
- **JetBrains Mono** — code/logs only
- **Never:** serif on body text, labels, data, or numbers
- **Tabular figures** on every number (KPIs, prices, counts)

**Type scale tokens** (all in [app/globals.css](app/globals.css)):
`display` 52px serif / `page-title` 36px serif / `kpi` 52px Inter 800 / `h2` 24px 700 / `h3` 16px 700 / `body` 14px 400 / `label` 11px 700 uppercase `tracking-0.08em` / `caption` 12px 400

**Logo & Mark**
- Lowercase italic `i` in filled tile — single shape works at every size
- Lockups: horizontal (tile + "InkOS" + "Studio OS" subtitle), wordmark only, stacked mono
- Clear space: padding ≥ 0.5× tile height on all sides
- Favicon 16–64px = mark only, no wordmark

# InkOS — Invite Team Member Modal Redesign

## Context

The user opened `/artists/new` and hit the **Invite a Team Member** modal. The modal is
cramped: `max-w-md` (448px) with 5 role cards stacked vertically plus email, commission,
invite link preview, and personal message all in one tall column. On a 1440px laptop the
modal's content overflows past the fold and every role decision requires scrolling.

The modal lives at [components/settings/team/InviteModal.tsx](components/settings/team/InviteModal.tsx).
The codebase already has `<FormLayout>` / `<FormLayout.Section>` at
[components/shared/FormLayout.tsx](components/shared/FormLayout.tsx) used on settings
pages, but the modal doesn't use it — it's a flat `space-y-5` stack.

**Goal:** widen the modal to `sm:max-w-[720px]`, put the 5 role cards in a 2-column
grid, group fields into visual sections with on-brand hierarchy, and apply brand rules
(Instrument Serif title, Rust-earned active role state, tabular-nums on commission %).
No logic changes — state management (inline `useState`), validation (inline email
regex), server-side token RPC all stay. This is a **visual + structural** pass.

---

## Recommended Approach

### Change 1 — Widen the modal

**File:** [components/settings/team/InviteModal.tsx:155](components/settings/team/InviteModal.tsx#L155)

- `max-w-md` → `sm:max-w-[720px]` on `<DialogContent>`
- Also add `max-h-[calc(100vh-4rem)] overflow-y-auto` so tall content scrolls internally instead of pushing the whole viewport

Rationale: 720px is the sweet spot for a form-heavy modal — fits the 2-column role grid
(2×320px + gap) and still sits comfortably on a 13" laptop without spanning edge-to-edge.
Existing modals in the app cap at 520px; this one carries more content and justifies more
width.

### Change 2 — Title uses Instrument Serif

**File:** same file, `<DialogTitle>` around line 157

- Current: default sans title.
- New: `className="font-serif text-[26px] font-normal leading-tight tracking-tight"`

Matches brand rule #4 — "Serif shows up in moments, not paragraphs." Modal title is
exactly that moment. Mirrors the dashboard hero treatment.

Description subtext (if any) stays Inter/body size, Stone color.

### Change 3 — 2-column role grid

**File:** role picker block at lines 184–216

Replace the stacked RadioGroup with:

```tsx
<RadioGroup
  value={role}
  onValueChange={setRole}
  className="grid grid-cols-1 gap-2 sm:grid-cols-2"
>
  {visibleRoles.map((r, i) => (
    <RoleCard
      key={r.value}
      role={r}
      selected={role === r.value}
      // Last card (odd index) spans both cols on even N+1 to avoid a lonely half-row
      className={cn(i === visibleRoles.length - 1 && visibleRoles.length % 2 === 1 && 'sm:col-span-2')}
    />
  ))}
</RadioGroup>
```

- For non-owner users (4 visible roles): clean 2×2 grid.
- For owner users (5 visible roles): 2×2 + last card spans full width — avoids the
  orphan half-slot.

**RoleCard styling** (inline, not a separate file — keep scope tight):
- `h-auto min-h-[88px]` — roomier tap target + vertical breathing
- Icon at top-left (`h-4 w-4 text-muted-foreground`)
- Label: Inter 14px `font-semibold`
- Description: 12px `text-muted-foreground leading-snug`
- Selected state: `border-destructive` (Rust, per brand rule 2 — "active state, live
  indicator, or critical anchor" — selection is an active anchor) + `bg-destructive/[0.04]`
  faint tint
- Unselected hover: `hover:border-border hover:bg-muted/30`

### Change 4 — Group fields into FormLayout sections

**File:** same modal body

Restructure the form children from flat `space-y-5` into sectioned blocks. Since
FormLayout's 2-col section layout (240px label + content) doesn't fit inside a modal,
use a simpler section pattern inside the modal: **section heading** (11px uppercase
tracked Stone) + divider + content. Three sections:

1. **"WHO"** — Email + Role grid
2. **"COMPENSATION"** — Commission % (conditional on `role === 'artist'`) — the existing
   animated reveal stays
3. **"INVITATION"** — Invite link preview + Personal message

Between sections: `border-t border-border/60 pt-5 mt-5` (no full divider — just a hairline
at the top of each new section).

Commission input: add `tabular-nums` class (brand rule — tabular figures on every number).

### Change 5 — Invite link preview polish

**File:** invite link preview block at lines 239–260

- The URL text: `font-mono text-[12px]` (per brand book — code/URLs use JetBrains Mono).
- Container: `bg-muted/30` with `border-border/60` (already close; just tighten alignment).
- Copy button: match the `HeaderBookingLinkButton` tooltip pattern — icon-only with
  hover toast on copy.

### Change 6 — Sticky footer

**File:** footer actions at lines 274–282

- Wrap actions in `<div className="sticky bottom-0 -mx-6 -mb-6 flex items-center justify-end gap-2 border-t border-border/60 bg-background px-6 py-4 mt-2">`
- Cancel = ghost button, Send Invite = primary (Onyx, which it already is).

Rationale: with a taller modal, keeping the CTA visible while scrolling is a UX must.

---

## Files to Modify

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| [components/settings/team/InviteModal.tsx](components/settings/team/InviteModal.tsx) | Full visual restructure: width 720px, serif title, 2-col role grid with Rust selection, sectioned body, sticky footer |

**Reference (no edits):**
- [components/ui/dialog.tsx](components/ui/dialog.tsx) — Base UI dialog primitive (already accepts width override via className)
- [components/shared/FormLayout.tsx](components/shared/FormLayout.tsx) — section pattern inspiration; we'll use a simpler variant inside the modal rather than reuse directly
- [components/app/sidebar/HeaderBookingLinkButton.tsx](components/app/sidebar/HeaderBookingLinkButton.tsx) — copy-link-with-tooltip pattern to mirror for the invite link preview
- [app/api/team-invites/route.ts](app/api/team-invites/route.ts) — server schema + RPC — NOT TOUCHED

---

## Brand Rule Check

- **Rule 1 — Editorial polish:** serif modal title, Stone section headers, hairline
  dividers, tabular numbers. ✅
- **Rule 2 — Rust is earned:** selected role card border-Rust + tint. "Active anchor" =
  qualifying use. ✅
- **Rule 3 — Onyx buttons carry workflow:** Send Invite stays Onyx. Cancel stays ghost. ✅
- **Rule 4 — Serif in moments, not paragraphs:** modal title only. Body stays Inter. ✅

---

## Verification

1. **Typecheck:** `pnpm typecheck` — clean.
2. **Dev:** `pnpm dev`, open `/artists/new`, click the invite trigger.
3. **Visual — desktop ≥1280px:**
   - Modal width is ~720px, centered, does not touch viewport edges.
   - Title renders in Instrument Serif, italic-capable weight 400.
   - 5 role cards visible in 2×2 + full-width last-row (owner user) OR 2×2 (non-owner).
   - Selecting "Artist" reveals the Commission % block under a "COMPENSATION" section
     header; 30 displays with tabular spacing.
   - Invite link chip renders in mono font; copy button toasts on click.
   - Footer sticks to modal bottom while scrolling the middle content.
4. **Visual — laptop 1024px:** modal is `sm:max-w-[720px]` — still fits (viewport > 720+64
   margin).
5. **Visual — ≤640px (mobile):** grid collapses to 1 column; width becomes
   `max-w-[calc(100%-2rem)]` per Base UI default; scrollable.
6. **Functional regression:**
   - Submit flow unchanged — RPC `create_team_invite` still called.
   - Email validation still runs inline.
   - Commission % field still only appears for `role === 'artist'`.
   - Owner role only visible to owner — `visibleRoles` filter unchanged.
7. **A11y:** tab order: email → role radios (arrow-key navigable) → commission →
   personal message → Cancel → Send. Role cards keep `<RadioGroupItem>` primitive so
   screen readers still announce "radio group, 5 options".

The user opened `/artists/new` and hit the **Invite a Team Member** modal. The modal is

invite link preview, and personal message all in one tall column. On a 1440px laptop the
modal's content overflows past the fold and every role decision requires scrolling.

The modal lives at [components/settings/team/InviteModal.tsx](components/settings/team/InviteModal.tsx).
The codebase already has `<FormLayout>` / `<FormLayout.Section>` at
[components/shared/FormLayout.tsx](components/shared/FormLayout.tsx) used on settings
pages, but the modal doesn't use it — it's a flat `space-y-5` stack.

**Goal:** widen the modal to `sm:max-w-[720px]`, put the 5 role cards in a 2-column
grid, group fields into visual sections with on-brand hierarchy, and apply brand rules
(Instrument Serif title, Rust-earned active role state, tabular-nums on commission %).
No logic changes — state management (inline `useState`), validation (inline email
regex), server-side token RPC all stay. This is a **visual + structural** pass.

---

## Recommended Approach

### Change 1 — Widen the modal

**File:** [components/settings/team/InviteModal.tsx:155](components/settings/team/InviteModal.tsx#L155)

- `max-w-md` → `sm:max-w-[720px]` on `<DialogContent>`
- Also add `max-h-[calc(100vh-4rem)] overflow-y-auto` so tall content scrolls internally instead of pushing the whole viewport

Rationale: 720px is the sweet spot for a form-heavy modal — fits the 2-column role grid
(2×320px + gap) and still sits comfortably on a 13" laptop without spanning edge-to-edge.
Existing modals in the app cap at 520px; this one carries more content and justifies more
width.

### Change 2 — Title uses Instrument Serif

**File:** same file, `<DialogTitle>` around line 157

- Current: default sans title.
- New: `className="font-serif text-[26px] font-normal leading-tight tracking-tight"`

Matches brand rule #4 — "Serif shows up in moments, not paragraphs." Modal title is
exactly that moment. Mirrors the dashboard hero treatment.

Description subtext (if any) stays Inter/body size, Stone color.

### Change 3 — 2-column role grid

**File:** role picker block at lines 184–216

Replace the stacked RadioGroup with:

```tsx
<RadioGroup
  value={role}
  onValueChange={setRole}
  className="grid grid-cols-1 gap-2 sm:grid-cols-2"
>
  {visibleRoles.map((r, i) => (
    <RoleCard
      key={r.value}
      role={r}
      selected={role === r.value}
      // Last card (odd index) spans both cols on even N+1 to avoid a lonely half-row
      className={cn(i === visibleRoles.length - 1 && visibleRoles.length % 2 === 1 && 'sm:col-span-2')}
    />
  ))}
</RadioGroup>
```

- For non-owner users (4 visible roles): clean 2×2 grid.
- For owner users (5 visible roles): 2×2 + last card spans full width — avoids the
  orphan half-slot.

- `h-auto min-h-[88px]` — roomier tap target + vertical breathing
- Icon at top-left (`h-4 w-4 text-muted-foreground`)
- Label: Inter 14px `font-semibold`
- Description: 12px `text-muted-foreground leading-snug`
- Selected state: `border-destructive` (Rust, per brand rule 2 — "active state, live
  indicator, or critical anchor" — selection is an active anchor) + `bg-destructive/[0.04]`
  faint tint
- Unselected hover: `hover:border-border hover:bg-muted/30`

### Change 4 — Group fields into FormLayout sections

**File:** same modal body

Restructure the form children from flat `space-y-5` into sectioned blocks. Since
FormLayout's 2-col section layout (240px label + content) doesn't fit inside a modal,
use a simpler section pattern inside the modal: **section heading** (11px uppercase
